ja: だいひゃくじゅうななかい

p.src: Lady Wang sent someone to summon Baochai for a consultation. When Baoyu heard that a monk was outside, he hurried alone to the front of the house, crying out distractedly, “Where is my master?” After calling for a long while without seeing any monk, he had no choice but to go outside. There he saw Li Gui barring the monk’s way and refusing to let him enter. Baoyu said, “Mother has asked me to invite my master inside.” Hearing this, Li Gui released his hold, and the monk swaggered inside. Baoyu saw that the monk looked just as he had when Baoyu lay near death, and at once began to understand. He stepped forward, bowed, and repeatedly said, “Master, your disciple is late in welcoming you.” The monk said, “I do not want your hospitality. I want only the silver; bring it to me, and I shall leave.” To Baoyu, these words did not sound like those of an enlightened man. Yet, seeing the monk’s head covered with sores and his whole body filthy and clothed in rags, he thought, “From ancient times it has been said, ‘A true immortal does not reveal his form, and one who reveals his form is no true immortal.’ I must not let him pass before my very eyes. For now I shall promise him the silver in thanks and sound him out.” He therefore said, “Master, there is no need for impatience. My mother is making the arrangements now. Please sit down and wait a little while. May your disciple ask whether you have come from the Land of Illusion?” The monk replied, “What Land of Illusion? I merely come from whence I came and go whither I go! I came to return your jade to you. But first let me ask you: where did that jade come from?” Baoyu could not answer at once. The monk laughed. “You do not even know where you yourself came from, yet you come asking me!” Baoyu was naturally quick-witted, and after receiving enlightenment he had long since seen through the illusions of the mortal world; only his own true origins remained unknown to him. When he heard the monk ask about the jade, it was as though he had received a blow to the head. He said, “Then you need no silver. I shall return the jade to you.” The monk laughed. “It is indeed time you returned it to me.”

p.src: Without another word, Baoyu ran back inside. Reaching his own courtyard, he saw that Baochai, Xiren, and the others had all gone to Lady Wang’s quarters. He hastened to his bedside, took the jade, and came out again. He ran straight into Xiren coming the other way, nearly knocking her over and giving her a fright. She said, “Her Ladyship said you were doing very well keeping the monk company while she arranged to give him some silver. What have you come back here for?” Baoyu said, “Go quickly and tell Mother there is no need to arrange any silver. I need only return this jade to him.” At this, Xiren hurriedly seized hold of him and said, “You must never do that! That jade is your very life. If he takes it away, you will fall ill again.” Baoyu said, “I shall not fall ill again. I have awakened to understanding now; what use have I for that jade?” He shook himself free of Xiren and made to leave. In her desperation, Xiren chased after him, crying, “Come back! I have something to tell you.” Baoyu turned his head and said, “There is nothing more to say.” Heedless of everything, Xiren ran after him, crying, “When the jade was lost last time, it nearly cost me my life! You have only just recovered it, and now you mean to take it away. Then neither you nor I will survive! If you mean to return it to him, you will have to wait until I am dead!” As she spoke, she caught up and seized him. Baoyu, growing exasperated, said, “Whether you die or not, I am returning it!” He gave Xiren a violent shove and tried to pull away. But Xiren had wound both hands around Baoyu’s sash and would not let go; weeping and shouting, she sank to the ground. Hearing the commotion, the maids inside hurried over. Seeing the two of them in such a state, they heard Xiren cry, “Go and tell Her Ladyship quickly! Second Master Bao means to take the jade and return it to the monk!” One of the maids flew to report to Lady Wang. Baoyu grew still angrier and tried to pry Xiren’s hands loose, but fortunately she endured the pain and refused to release him. Inside the room, Zijuan heard that Baoyu meant to give the jade away. More alarmed than anyone else, she completely forgot her usual resolve to keep aloof from him and rushed out to help hold him fast. Though Baoyu was a man and struggled with all his strength, the two women clung to him for dear life and would not let go, so he could not break free. He sighed and said, “You cling to me for dear life over a piece of jade. What would you do if I myself were to leave alone?” At these words, Xiren and Zijuan could not help bursting into loud sobs. While they were still locked in this struggle, Lady Wang and Baochai hurried in. Seeing the scene before them, Lady Wang cried as she shouted, “Baoyu, have you gone mad again?”

p.src: When Baoyu saw Lady Wang arrive, he knew he could not get away, so he forced a smile and said, “This is nothing worth troubling you over, Mother. They are always making such a tremendous fuss. I said that monk was most unreasonable: he insisted on ten thousand taels of silver and would not accept a single tael less. I lost my temper and came in to fetch this jade and return it to him, telling him it was false and asking what use I had for it. Once he saw that we did not prize the jade, he would accept whatever we chose to give him, and that would settle the matter.” Lady Wang said, “I thought you truly meant to return it to him. If that was all, it would not have mattered. Why did you not explain it clearly to them? What a spectacle you made of them, weeping and shouting like that!” Baochai said, “If that is what you meant, it is acceptable enough. But if you really gave him the jade, that monk is such a strange fellow that the moment he got it, he might stir up some fresh trouble and throw the whole household into turmoil. Would that not be disastrous? As for the money, even if I have to sell my jewelry, it should still be enough.” Hearing this, Lady Wang said, “Very well. Let us do that for the time being.” Baoyu made no reply. Baochai stepped forward, took the jade from Baoyu’s hand, and said, “There is no need for you to go out. Mother and I will give him the money.” Baoyu said, “It is all right not to return the jade, but I must still see him face-to-face.” Xiren and the others still refused to release him, but Baochai made the final decision, saying, “Let him go. Leave him to do as he pleases.” Xiren had no choice but to let go. Baoyu laughed. “So all of you value the jade and not the man! Since you have released me, I shall follow him away. Let us see what good it does you to remain here guarding that piece of jade!” Xiren grew anxious again and wanted to seize him, but in the presence of Lady Wang and Baochai, she could not behave with undue familiarity. At that very moment, Baoyu shook himself free and left. Xiren hurriedly told a young maid to pass word at the inner gate to Beiming and the others: “Tell the servants outside to keep an eye on Master Bao. He has gone a little mad.” The young maid assented and went out.

p.src: Lady Wang, Baochai, and the others went inside and sat down. When they asked Xiren what had happened, she gave them a detailed account of what Baoyu had said. Lady Wang and Baochai were deeply uneasy. They sent someone out again to instruct the servants to attend Baoyu and listen carefully to what the monk said. The young maid returned with a message and reported to Lady Wang, “Master Bao really has gone a little mad. The pages outside say that since those inside will not give him the jade, there is nothing he can do about that; but now that he himself has come out, he is begging the monk to take him away.” On hearing this, Lady Wang exclaimed, “This is intolerable! What did the monk say?” The young maid replied, “The monk said he wanted the jade, not the man.” Baochai asked, “Does he no longer want the silver?” The young maid said, “I did not hear anything about it. Later, the monk and Master Bao were talking and laughing together. They said a great many things that the pages outside could scarcely understand.” Lady Wang said, “You stupid creatures! Even if you could not understand it, surely you could repeat what you heard.” Then she told the young maid, “Bring that page in here.” The young maid hurried out and brought the page in. He stood beneath the veranda and paid his respects through the window. Lady Wang asked, “You say you could not understand the monk’s conversation with Master Bao, but could you not at least repeat it?” The page replied, “We only heard them mention something called the ‘Great Waste Mountain’ and something called ‘Greensickness Peak.’ They also spoke of the ‘Realm of the Great Void’ and of ‘severing all worldly ties.’” Lady Wang did not understand these words either. But Baochai was so frightened that her eyes opened wide and she could not utter a word. Just as they were about to send someone out to drag Baoyu back inside, he came in grinning and said, “It is all settled! It is all settled!” Baochai remained frozen in astonishment. Lady Wang said, “What madness are you babbling now?” Baoyu replied, “Whenever I speak seriously, you call me mad. That monk and I have known each other all along. He merely came because he wanted to see me. He never truly wanted the silver; he merely meant to solicit an offering and form an auspicious bond. Once he had explained himself, he simply drifted away. So is that not a happy conclusion?” Lady Wang did not believe him and questioned the page again through the window. The page hurried out to question the gatekeepers, then returned and reported, “The monk has indeed gone. He said the ladies should set their minds at ease. ‘I never wanted the silver,’ he said. ‘I only wish Master Bao to visit me from time to time. In all things, one need only follow the course of affinity; everything has its own appointed principle.’” Lady Wang said, “So he is a good monk after all. Did you ask where he lives?” The gatekeeper replied, “Your servant did ask him. He said that our Master Bao knew.” Lady Wang asked Baoyu, “Where exactly does he live?”

p.src: Baoyu laughed. “That place is far away if you call it far, and close at hand if you call it near.” Before he could finish, Baochai said, “Come to your senses. You must not remain utterly lost in such fantasies. Now the master and mistress have only you to cherish, and the master has expressly told you to distinguish yourself through official advancement.” “Was I not speaking of distinction?” Baoyu replied. “You do not understand: ‘When one son enters religion, seven generations of his ancestors ascend to heaven.’” Hearing this, Lady Wang could not help growing heartsick. “How could our family be blessed with good fortune? Fourth Girl is forever declaring that she means to become a nun, and now another one has appeared. What is the use of my going on living such a life?” With that, she burst into loud sobs. Seeing Lady Wang so distressed, Baochai had no choice but to step forward and earnestly console her. Baoyu laughed. “I said one thing in jest, and Mother has taken it seriously again.” Lady Wang checked her weeping and said, “Are such things to be spoken as idle nonsense?” In the midst of this commotion, a maid came to report: “Second Master Lian has returned. His face is terribly changed, and he asks Madam to go back and speak with him.” Lady Wang was startled once more. “We shall make do as we are. Tell him to come in. His young aunt is an old relation too, so there is no need for her to withdraw.” Jia Lian entered and paid his respects to Lady Wang. Baochai came forward and exchanged greetings with Jia Lian as well. He reported, “I have just received a letter from my father saying that he is gravely ill and summoning me to him at once. If I delay, I fear I may not see him alive.” At these words, tears began to fall from his eyes. Lady Wang asked, “What illness does the letter say it is?” Jia Lian replied, “It says he first caught a chill, but that it has now developed into consumption. He is now in grave danger. A man was specially dispatched to travel here day and night, with word that if I delay another day or two, I shall not see him alive. That is why I have come to inform you, Aunt. I really must leave at once. The only trouble is that no one will be left to oversee the household. Qiang and Yun may be muddleheaded, but they are men, after all, and if anything happens outside, they can at least carry a message. There should be no particular trouble in my own quarters. Qiutong cried and clamored every day that she would not stay here, so I summoned her family and had them take her away. That has spared Ping’er a good deal of vexation. Although no one else is there to look after Qiaojie, it is fortunate that Ping’er is not unkind at heart. The girl understands what is going on, but her temper is even more unyielding than her mother’s. I beg you, Aunt, to instruct and discipline her from time to time.” As he spoke, his eyes reddened. He hurriedly pulled free the little silk handkerchief tied at his waist beside his betel-nut purse and wiped his eyes. Lady Wang said, “Her own grandmother is right there. Why entrust her to me?” Jia Lian said softly, “If Aunt speaks so, I deserve to be beaten to death on the spot.

p.src: There is nothing more I can say; I ask only that Aunt continue to care for me as you always have.” With that, he knelt down. Lady Wang’s eyes reddened too. “Get up quickly. We are mother and son speaking together—what are you doing this for? There is just one matter. The girl is grown now. If some misfortune should befall your father and you are detained there, and meanwhile a well-matched family comes with a marriage proposal, are we to wait for your return, or is your wife to decide?” Jia Lian replied, “Since the ladies are here at present, naturally you should decide. There is no need to wait for me.” Lady Wang said, “If you are going, write a formal note to inform Second Master. Tell him there is no one at home, and no one knows what may happen to your father. Ask him to conclude the Old Lady’s funeral arrangements as soon as possible and hurry home.” Jia Lian answered, “Yes,” and was about to leave when he turned back and reported, “There are still enough household servants to meet our needs, but the Garden is far too empty with no one living there. Baoyong has gone away with their master as well. As for the rooms where Aunt Xue stayed, Second Master Xue has moved back into his own quarters. All the rooms throughout the Garden stand empty and are much too poorly watched. Madam must have someone inspect them regularly. Green Lattice Nunnery was originally built on land belonging to our family. Now no one knows where Miaoyu has gone, and the nun in charge dares not decide on her own what to do with the property there. She asks that someone from the mansion manage it.” Lady Wang said, “We cannot even put our own affairs in order. How can we find time for matters outside the household? Whatever happens, do not let Fourth Girl hear of this. If she learns of it, she will start clamoring again about becoming a nun. Think what kind of family ours is! If a perfectly good daughter of the house became a nun, what a scandal that would be!” Jia Lian said, “Had Aunt not mentioned it, I would not have dared speak. Fourth Sister belongs to the eastern mansion, after all. She has no parents; her own brother is away, and her sister-in-law has little authority over her. I have heard that several times she threatened to take her own life. Since her heart is already set upon it, if we stubbornly restrain her and she should later truly kill herself, that would be worse than letting her become a nun.” Lady Wang listened, nodded, and said, “This matter truly leaves me in a difficult position. I cannot decide it either. We shall simply leave it to her elder sister-in-law.”

I cannot decide it either. We shall simply leave it to her elder sister-in-law.”

p.src: Only after saying a few more words did Jia Lian leave. He summoned the household servants and gave them thorough instructions, wrote his letter, and packed for the journey, while Ping’er and the others naturally gave him many parting admonitions. Qiaojie alone was inconsolably grief-stricken. Jia Lian also wished to entrust her to Wang Ren, but Qiaojie would have none of it. When she heard that Yun and Qiang had been given charge of outside affairs, she felt even more unhappy, though she could not bring herself to say so. She could only see her father off and then live with Ping’er, conducting herself with the utmost caution. Since Xifeng’s death, Feng’er and Xiaohong had taken leave or reported sick. Ping’er wanted to bring over one of the girls from her own family, partly to keep Qiaojie company and partly to help look after her. But after considering everyone, she could think of no suitable person. Only Xiluan and Fourth Girl had once been especial favorites of Grandmother Jia; yet Fourth Girl had recently married, while Xiluan too was betrothed and would soon leave her family to wed. So Ping’er had no choice but to abandon the idea.

p.src: Now, after Jia Yun and Jia Qiang had seen Jia Lian off, they went inside to pay their respects to Ladies Xing and Wang. The two of them took turns lodging in the outer study, romping with the servants by day; sometimes they invited several friends to a round-robin drinking party, and even gathered to gamble, all without anyone in the inner quarters knowing. One day Uncle Xing and Wang Ren came by. Seeing Jia Yun and Jia Qiang living there and knowing how lively their company was, they too used the pretext of keeping watch over the place to set up gambling games and drink frequently in the outer study. As for the few dependable servants, Jia Zheng had taken some with him and several more had followed Jia Lian, leaving only the sons and nephews of the Lai, Lin, and other households. Those young men had long been accustomed, through their parents' good fortune, to eating and drinking their fill; how could they understand the principles of managing a household and planning its affairs? Moreover, with their elders all away, they were horses without bridles; and with two collateral masters egging them on, there was nothing they would not gladly do. Their uproar threw the Rongguo Mansion into utter disorder, with neither rank nor boundary respected. Jia Qiang even wanted to draw Baoyu into their company, but Jia Yun stopped him, saying, “Master Bao is an unlucky fellow. There is no need to bother with him. One year I proposed an excellent match for him: her father was a tax official away from home, her family owned several pawnshops, and the girl was prettier than a fairy. I went to all the trouble of writing him a detailed letter, but who knew he would have no such good fortune—” At this point he looked around, and seeing no one nearby, continued, “In his heart, he had long been enamored of this Second Aunt of ours. Have you not heard about a certain Miss Lin as well? He drove her to die of lovesickness—everyone knows it. But never mind that; each has his own destined match. Who would have thought that he would instead take offense at me over it and scarcely acknowledge me afterward? He must imagine that everyone depends upon someone else's reflected glory.” Jia Qiang nodded when he heard this and at last abandoned the idea.

p.src: Neither of them knew that, since meeting the monk, Baoyu had desired to sever all ties with the mortal world. For one thing, he dared not indulge his whims in Lady Wang's presence, and he had already grown rather distant from Baochai, Xiren, and the others. The maids, unaware of this, still tried to tease him, but Baoyu paid them no attention at all. Nor did he give any thought to household affairs. Lady Wang and Baochai often urged him to study, whereupon he pretended to apply himself to his books while thinking only of how the monk might lead him into that immortal realm. Everyone he encountered seemed worldly in his eyes, making life at home unbearable; in his leisure he preferred to converse with Xichun. The two understood each other, and their conversations made his resolve firmer still. How could he trouble himself about Jia Huan, Jia Lan, and the rest? As Jia Huan's father was away, Concubine Zhao was dead, and Lady Wang paid him little heed, he fell in with Jia Qiang's set. Caiyun often tried to remonstrate with him, but Jia Huan only abused her in return. Seeing Baoyu grow more deranged than ever, Yuchuan had long since told her mother that she wished to petition for release from service. Now Baoyu and Jia Huan, the two brothers, each had his own peculiar temper, and their behavior made everyone ignore them. Jia Lan alone followed his mother's guidance and studied diligently, writing essays and sending them to the school to seek Dai Ru's instruction. But as Dai Ru had lately been confined to bed by age and illness, Jia Lan had no choice but to labor on by himself. Li Wan had always been quiet and reserved. Apart from paying her respects to Lady Wang and occasionally visiting Baochai, she never went anywhere, devoting herself solely to overseeing Jia Lan's studies. Thus, though many people still lived in the Rong Mansion, each went his own way, and no one was willing to take charge of anyone else. Jia Huan, Jia Qiang, and the others grew ever more outrageous, secretly pawning and selling household property among countless other offenses. Jia Huan went further still, frequenting prostitutes, gambling recklessly, and stopping at nothing.

p.src: One day Uncle Xing and Wang Ren were drinking in the Jia family's outer study. Growing merry, they summoned several singing girls to sing, drink, and press wine upon the company. Jia Qiang said, “Your revelry is much too vulgar. I shall propose a drinking game.” “Very well,” everyone replied. Jia Qiang said, “Let us pass the cup with the word ‘moon.’ I shall begin with the word ‘moon,’ and whoever is reached by the count must drink and supply both an opening and a closing verse. Everyone must obey the master of the game; anyone who refuses shall be fined three large cups.” Everyone agreed. Jia Qiang drank the cup with which the game was inaugurated, then said, “Pass the feathered goblet and grow drunk beneath the moon.” They drank in order, and the count fell upon Jia Huan. Jia Qiang said, “Your opening must contain the word ‘cassia.’” Jia Huan replied, “‘Silent cold dew moistens the cassia blossoms.’ And what of the closing verse?” Jia Qiang said, “Give us the word ‘fragrance.’” Jia Huan said, “Heavenly fragrance drifts beyond the clouds.” Uncle Xing said, “What a bore, what a bore! Since when did you know anything about letters, putting on such a refined air? This is no amusement at all; it is positively exasperating. Let us dispense with all this and play finger-guessing instead: the loser drinks and sings, and we shall call it ‘Bitterness upon Bitterness.’ If anyone cannot sing, a joke will do, so long as it is amusing.” “Very well,” everyone said. They then began playing finger-guessing in a disorderly fashion. Wang Ren lost, drank a cup, and sang a song. Everyone applauded, and they began another round. One of the singing girls lost and sang something about “Miss, dear miss, how radiant your charms.” Later Uncle Xing lost. When everyone demanded a song, he said, “I cannot sing. Let me tell a joke instead.” Jia Qiang said, “If it does not make us laugh, you must still pay a forfeit.” Uncle Xing drank a cup and began: “Gentlemen, listen. In a country village there stood a Temple of the Primordial Emperor, with a shrine to the local earth god beside it. His Lordship the Primordial Emperor often summoned the earth god for a chat. One day the Temple of the Primordial Emperor was robbed, so he ordered the earth god to investigate. The earth god reported, ‘There are no thieves in this district. The divine generals must have been careless, allowing thieves from elsewhere to steal the things.’ The Primordial Emperor said, ‘Nonsense! You are the god of this land. If a theft occurs, whom should I question if not you? Instead of catching the thief, you accuse my divine generals of carelessness?’ The earth god reported, ‘Though there may indeed have been carelessness, the fundamental cause is the temple's poor geomancy.’ The Primordial Emperor said, ‘So you know how to judge geomancy?’ The earth god replied, ‘Permit this humble deity to take a look.’ The earth god looked about in every direction for a while, then returned and reported, ‘The two red doors behind Your Lordship's seat provide very poor security. Behind my own seat is a brick wall, so naturally nothing can be stolen from me. All will be well if Your Lordship likewise has the space behind you walled up from now on.’”

p.src: Lord Emperor Xuan thought this made sense and ordered the divine generals to send men to build a wall. The divine generals sighed. “Nowadays we do not receive so much as a single stick of incense. Where are we to find bricks, mortar, or laborers to build a wall?” Lord Emperor Xuan was at a loss. He told the divine generals to use their magic, but none of them had any idea what to do. Then General Tortoise, who stood at Lord Emperor Xuan’s feet, rose and said, “You are all useless, but I have an idea. Take down the red gate, and at night I shall block its entrance with my belly. Surely that will serve as a wall?” The divine generals all agreed. “Excellent! It will cost nothing, and it is convenient and sturdy too.” And so General Tortoise took on the duty, and peace was restored. Who would have thought that a few days later, something else would go missing from the temple? The divine generals summoned the local earth god and said, “You told us that once a wall was built, nothing would be stolen. Why are things still disappearing now that we have one?” “This wall cannot have been built securely,” replied the earth god. “Go and see for yourself,” said the divine generals. The earth god looked and saw that it was indeed a fine wall. How, then, could anything have gone wrong? He felt it with his hand and exclaimed, “I took it for a real wall—how was I to know it was a sham wall?”” Everyone burst out laughing when they heard this. Jia Qiang could not help laughing either. “Well done, you silly old uncle! I never insulted you, so why did you insult me? Bring a cup at once and fine him one great cupful!” Uncle Xing drank it and was already becoming tipsy. After several more rounds, they all grew drunk. Uncle Xing spoke ill of his elder sister, while Wang Ren spoke ill of his younger sister, both of them using the most vicious language. Hearing them, Jia Huan took advantage of his drunken spirits to disparage Xifeng too, describing how harshly she treated them and how she trampled them underfoot. “Anyone who calls himself human ought to show some kindness,” said the others. Miss Feng relied on the Old Lady’s favor to behave so ruthlessly, but now her own tail has been singed. She has only one daughter left, and that girl may well suffer retribution before her very eyes.” Jia Yun remembered how badly Xifeng had treated him, and how Qiaojie cried whenever she saw him, so he too let his tongue run wild. It was Jia Qiang who finally said, “Let us drink. Why talk about other people?” The two drinking companions asked, “How old is this young lady? What does she look like?” “She is very pretty indeed,” replied Jia Qiang. And she is thirteen or fourteen years old.” “What a pity that such a girl was born into a great household like this,” said one of the companions. “Had she been born to a humble family, her parents and brothers might all have gained office and made their fortunes.” “How so?” they all asked. The companion said, “There is a prince from an outlying domain who is most affectionate by nature and now wishes to choose a consort. If she met his requirements, her parents and brothers could all accompany her.

p.src: Just then, two young men from the Lai and Lin families entered from outside, saying, “You gentlemen seem to be enjoying yourselves!” Everyone rose. “Eldest and Third, why have you come so late? You have kept us waiting!” The two replied, “This morning we heard a rumor that fresh trouble had broken out in our household. We were worried and hurried inside to make inquiries, but it turned out not to concern us.” “If it did not concern us, that should have settled it. Why did you not come straight here?” the others asked. “Although it did not concern us directly, it was still somewhat connected with us,” said the two. Do you know who it was? His Excellency Jia Yucun. When we went in today, we saw him in chains. They said he was to be taken before the Three Judicial Offices for interrogation. Since he often visited our household, we feared there might be some trouble, so we followed along to find out more.” “Eldest is certainly conscientious,” said Jia Yun. “It was only right to investigate. Sit down and have a cup before telling us the rest.” After exchanging courtesies, the two sat down. As they drank, they said, “His Excellency Yucun is a capable man and adept at currying favor. He had risen to a high position, but he was greedy for money, and someone impeached him on several charges of extorting his subordinates. The present Son of Heaven is supremely wise and benevolent, but the very word ‘corruption’ enrages him—whether it means oppressing the common people or abusing power to bully the innocent. He therefore issued an edict ordering Yucun’s arrest and interrogation. If the charges are proved, I fear he will not escape punishment. But if the allegations prove false, the accuser will be in an awkward position too. These truly are good times: if fortune only grants a man an official post, he can do well.” “Your elder brother is one of fortune’s favorites,” said the others. “Is it not good enough that he is now a county magistrate?” The young man from the Lai family replied, “Although my brother is a county magistrate, given his conduct, I fear there is no telling what may happen to him.” “Does he have long hands too?” they asked. The young man from the Lai family nodded, then raised his cup and drank. “What other news did you hear inside?” the others asked. “Nothing else,” the two replied. “We heard only that many pirates from the coastal regions had been captured and were likewise sent to the judicial offices for interrogation. Their questioning exposed many more bandits, some of whom had been hiding in the capital, gathering information and seizing opportunities to plunder households. Now they know that the high officials at court are masters of both civil and military affairs, loyally serving the throne, and that wherever they go, the bandits are swiftly wiped out.” “Since you heard that some were hiding in the capital, do you know whether our household’s burglary case came to light during the interrogation?” they asked. “We did not hear anything about that,” the two replied. We vaguely heard someone say that a man from the interior committed a crime in the capital, abducted a woman, and fled out to sea. When the woman resisted, the bandit killed her.

“Plenty of women were carried off,” the others said. “Why must it have been her?”
Jia Yun said, “There is some word of it.
Someone said the other day that a Taoist nun at her convent had dreamed she saw Miaoyu being murdered.”
They all laughed. “You can’t put any faith in dreams.”
Uncle Xing said, “Dream or no dream, never mind that. Let’s hurry up and eat.
Tonight we’ll play for really high stakes.”
The others readily agreed. When they had finished eating, they began gambling in earnest.

p.src: They gambled until well after the third watch, when a great commotion suddenly broke out in the inner apartments. They heard that Fourth Miss had quarrelled with Madam Zhen, cut off all her hair, and rushed to Lady Xing and Lady Wang to kowtow before them, begging to be allowed to become a nun and to be given a place for the purpose; if they refused, she declared, she would kill herself before their very eyes. Neither Lady Xing nor Lady Wang knew what to do, so they sent for Master Qiang and Second Master Yun. When Jia Yun heard what had happened, he realized that this was the resolve Xichun had formed when they were guarding the house that time and that she was unlikely to be dissuaded. He therefore consulted Jia Qiang. “The ladies have called us in, but this is not for us to decide. Besides, it would be improper for us to decide; all we can do is try to persuade her. If she will not listen, we shall simply have to let them do as they please. Let us agree on a letter to Second Uncle Lian; then we shall be free of responsibility.” Having settled on this plan, the two went in to see Lady Xing and Lady Wang and made a show of trying to dissuade Xichun. But Xichun was firmly resolved to enter religious life. She did not even ask to be allowed to leave the house, only for one or two quiet rooms where she could recite sutras and worship the Buddha. Seeing that neither man would take responsibility, and fearing that Xichun might kill herself, Madam You steeled herself to decide the matter. “Why don’t I simply take the blame for this? Then everyone can say that I, her sister-in-law, could not tolerate my husband’s younger sister and drove her into a nunnery, and that will be the end of it. As for letting her go outside, that is absolutely out of the question. But if she remains here at home, with both ladies present, let it be counted as my decision. Have young Qiang write a letter to your Master Zhen and Second Uncle Lian, and that will suffice.” Jia Qiang and the others assented. Whether Lady Xing and Lady Wang consented remains to be told in the next chapter.
